sections.heading: Callable and Future for Task Results

items: Callable is similar to Runnable but allows the task to return a result or throw an exception.
Future represents the result of an asynchronous computation. You can check whether the task is finished, cancel it, and get the result once it's done.
get(): Blocks and waits for the task to complete, then returns the result.
isDone(): Returns true if the task is completed.
isCancelled(): Returns true if the task was canceled.
cancel(): Attempts to cancel the task.

content.text: Here, get() blocks the main thread until the upload is complete and returns the result.
While synchronization using the synchronized keyword works, it has limitations:

items: Threads can be blocked indefinitely if they don't acquire the lock.
Synchronization can only be applied to methods or code blocks.
Allows acquiring and releasing locks at different places in code.
Can use tryLock() to avoid indefinite waiting.
lock(): Acquires the lock and blocks until it's available.
tryLock(): Attempts to acquire the lock without blocking.
unlock(): Releases the lock.

content.text: ReentrantLock is a specific implementation of Lock that:

items: Supports fairness (ensures the longest-waiting thread gets the lock first).
Can be used in multiple methods for better flexibility in acquiring and releasing locks.
